title: Ecosystem, certificates, and the bridge
blurb: Glossary, the mind map, certifications you can cite, and how CUCM, UCCX, UCCE, and Webex sit together.

lessons.title: Words that get projects in trouble
lessons.summary: The glossary in this lab is a short list of terms with citations. The dangerous pairs are the ones people treat as synonyms.

diagram.caption: If two features share a noun, look at the admin path.

flow.title: Stop a meeting when the noun is ambiguous

steps.label: Says queue
steps.detail: Ask whether they mean Calling > Features > Call Queue or a contact center queue.

steps.label: Says music
steps.detail: Calling music on hold is a location feature. Play Music is a flow activity.
steps.inspect: Do not reuse the file without checking both articles

steps.label: Says voicemail
steps.detail: Multi-tenant Calling voicemail is not Unity Connection. Dedicated Instance still deploys Unity Connection.

steps.label: Open the lab glossary
steps.detail: Each term has a source URL. If the live page renamed it, trust the page.

paragraphs: Trunk and route group. Dial plan and location dialing. Bot and virtual agent. Personal token and integration. HELD and caller ID.
The glossary is not exhaustive. It is the list this lab is willing to define.

cite.label: Trunks, route groups, and dial plans

paragraphs: ITU-T E.164 is the numbering plan. RFC 3966 is the tel URI. Webex Calling dial plans and the contact center voice article both care about +E.164.
A four-digit extension is not an E.164 number until a plan says how it maps.

quiz.why: Trust the live page if they differ.

lessons.title: Certifications and the course that is not the exam
lessons.summary: 300-830 CLCCE is a 90-minute exam. Passing it earns Cisco Certified Specialist - Collaboration Cloud Customer Experience and can count as a CCNP Collaboration concentration. CLWXCALL is a course, not that exam.
objectives: Use the official exam name and code
Leave price and unstated dates off your flashcards

diagram.caption: Exam page, topics page, course page. Three URLs.

flow.title: Read the exam page before you book

steps.label: Read 300-830 CLCCE
steps.detail: The exam page says it is 90 minutes, in English, and that passing earns the specialist certification and can meet a CCNP Collaboration concentration.
steps.inspect: Topics: telephony and call routing, tenant configuration and reporting, digital channels, advanced features and AI

steps.label: Open the learning network topics
steps.detail: The topics page this lab fetched lists 1.0 Telephony and Call Routing 30%, 2.0 Tenant Configuration and Reporting 30%, 3.0 Digital Channels 15%, 4.0 Advanced Features and AI 25%.

steps.label: Open CLWXCALL separately
steps.detail: Essentials of Webex Calling is a course. It is not the 300-830 exam.
steps.inspect: Do not put the course code on the exam registration

steps.label: Look them up live
steps.detail: The exam page shows a price. This lab does not put that number on a flashcard, because prices change. This lab also does not state a first-test date it could not read from the exam overview.
steps.inspect: Uncertainty: confirm dates on the live page

paragraphs: Cisco Certified Specialist - Collaboration Cloud Customer Experience, and it can be used toward CCNP Collaboration and recertification, per the exam page.
The CCNP Collaboration page is the parent certification. This lab does not invent a core-exam code.
A study aid with citations. It is not an official course and it does not include exam items.
The certification update article is where Cisco announces program changes. Read it when a code looks unfamiliar.

steps.label: Read the DI bullet before you sell embedding
steps.detail: The deployment-models page says the Webex Calling app can be embedded in Microsoft Teams for business calls, with logs, voicemail, and directory sync.

paragraphs: The voice channel article says Microsoft Teams integration for Webex Contact Center needs +E.164 on the local gateway and the full Control Hub trunk, route group, and location routing.
That is a gateway requirement, not one of the four CRM templates.

lessons.title: The bridge from CUCM, UCCX, and UCCE
lessons.summary: Unified CM can remain, move to Dedicated Instance, or migrate users to multi-tenant Calling. Contact center scripts are rebuilt. The admin door for all of the cloud pieces is Control Hub.
objectives: Keep UCCX and UCCE on their product pages until the redesign

diagram.caption: Three destinations. Do not pretend they are one project.

steps.label: Read the tar
steps.detail: Users, devices, shared groups, eligibility. CDR if you need usage.

steps.label: CSV, locations, PSTN, 933
steps.detail: Park and pickup may need the Python script. Voicemail messages do not come along.

steps.label: Activate, DNS, interop, cross-launch
steps.detail: Unity Connection exists here. CER wording depends on the page. Hypothetical models are not a customer.

steps.label: New flow, new queues, new desktop
steps.detail: No cited script import. Enterprise has its own docs.

paragraphs: Unified Communications Manager, Unified CCX, and Unified CCE keep their own Cisco support series. Webex does not retire those pages because a cloud offer exists.
Link them when the source system is still in production.

sections.h: One organization can hold more than one destination
paragraphs: The deployment-models page describes mixes of multi-tenant and Dedicated Instance. That mix needs the interop trunk.
Contact center can sit beside both. It is still not a Calling call queue.

lessons.title: Use the studio as a capstone
